articleTitle: Fire Rated Enclosures – A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper is a case study from the Hebron Offshore Oil Platform located in Atlantic Canada focusing on fire resistant medium voltage enclosures that were supplied for the seawater lift pumps and fire water pumps. The purpose of the paper is to show where fire resistant enclosures may be utilized and to detail the testing involved in achieving fire resistance with the enclosures for the Hebron Platform.

articleTitle: Introduction to the New Standards — IEEE STD 844.3™-2019 /CSA C22.2 No. 293.3-19 and IEEE STD 844.4™-2019/CSA C293.4-19 for Impedance Heating of Pipelines and Equipment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Through a joint standards development process between the Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE) and the Canadian Standards Association (CSA), two new standards are now completed. These new standards are a certification standard, IEEE Std 844.3™-2019/CSA C22.2 No. 293.3-19 (Standard for Impedance Heating of Pipelines and Equipment — General, Testing, Marking and Documentation Requirements), and an application guide standard, IEEE Std 844.4™-2019/CSA C22.2 No. C293.4-19 (Standard for Impedance Heating of Pipelines and Equipment — Application Guide for Design, Installation, Testing, Commissioning and Maintenance). These standards detail requirements that have been added or clarified in the impedance heating system certification process. This paper also summarizes applications as well as new recommended installation practices included in the application guide.

articleTitle: Unique New Cooling Technology for Refinery Use : Copyright Material IEEE Paper No. PCIC-2021-35
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Energy and water use for cooling in refineries are a significant cost and environmental challenge. Some estimates are evaporation in cooling towers use about 1/3 of makeup water for the cooling tower. An invention [1] developed by researchers at Stanford University may alleviate both energy consumption and water usage in refineries. This cooling technology uses a band in the atmosphere infrared spectrum that has minimal attenuation of this wavelength. Prototypes can significantly cool fluid below ambient during the day with incident sun on a panel.The atmosphere is transparent to radiation from 8 to 13 micrometers, and this allows light in this wavelength band to escape our atmosphere to outer space. This is done using a "nano photonic radiative cooling" surface made on a film that can be fabricated in square meter sizes. Currently the system can radiate about 100 to 400 watts/sq. meter depending on ambient temperatures. Current photovoltaic solar can produce about 200 watts/sq. meter with an input of about 1000 watts per sq. meter. The current prototype systems have the same form factor as solar panels; so much of the "rest of plant" is already designed. The panels provide heat rejection 24/7 and as a result, can save more energy than a solar panel can generate for the same area when connected to cooling loads that are on for more than 8 hours in a day.This paper examines refinery statistics for water and energy usage, cooling requirements and electrical usage for the cooling. It then estimates the efficacy of this new technology with its prospective improvements in the operation of refineries and process plants in both water conservation and energy use.

articleTitle: Comparative Assessment of Low Voltage Motor Ride-Through Solutions for Critical Processes in the Oil and Gas Industry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Voltage sags initiated by utility transmission system faults causes nuisance trips of low voltage (LV) motors due to contactors dropping off as a result of the under voltage condition. Since voltage disturbances by utility system cannot be prevented, it is essential to mitigate the impact of LV motors trips on critical process systems in the oil and gas industry such as lubrication and shaft-sealing systems. To address this challenge, several ride-through solutions were evaluated in terms of impact on motor performance and motor controller design. A simulation model was developed using PSCAD software to assess motor performance and subsequent current and torque profiles, associated with various ride-through solutions. The reliability and safety aspects of modifications associated with different ride-through solutions were evaluated, as well as, benchmarked with relevant international standards and industrial practices.

articleTitle: Change Is Continuous: A Refinery Restart E&I Design Case Study
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Changes with technology, hardware, cable schedules, industry standards, and processes are happening at an unprecedented pace. This paper will provide an overview and discussion of the most common factors within the E/l scope that can cause project delays, cost overruns, ongoing maintenance risks and other challenges. Further, this paper will discuss design practices for electrical buildings, along with equipment and cable management that will improve efficiencies associated with design, construction and long-term maintenance. The paper will conclude with a case study from an owner perspective that demonstrates the risks of continuous change and how these risks were mitigated with standardized electrical designs.

articleTitle: The Practical Impact of Area Classification on Trace Heating Cost
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Establishing area classifications for new plant construction during Front End Engineering Design (FEED) includes the addressing of the Auto Ignition Temperature (AIT) of hazardous gases expected for each area classification. A detailed approach often involves multiple area classifications within an area of a new plant. Conversely, the common industry practice that applies a blanket temperature rating (T-rating), such as T3, may increase Electrical Trace Heating (EHT) associated costs by not representing the true expected AIT of the combustible gases present in the plant. This paper will demonstrate how investing time to accurately prepare an area classification study for a plant can reduce total costs of heat trace ownership through savings because of product selection and design, as well as construction. Examples from a project process unit will address trace heating optimization by comparing the EHT design for an area classification drawing with detailed AIT information against the described common industry blanket T-rating practice, and showing associated Total Installed Cost (TIC) savings.

articleTitle: Innovative Cooling of Medium Voltage Drives In E-House
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The installation of air-cooled adjustable speed drives in an enclosed building can be a challenging task. The task increases in complexity when the installation involves drives of large power ratings that generate substantial heat and require large amounts of circulating air volume. Utilization of the waste hot air exhaust from the drive to maintain building temperature set point and diversion of hot air to the outside of the building while maintaining airflow to meet drive requirements can pose many challenges. This paper will discuss the challenges encountered during design, manufacturing, and testing of the complete system and delivery of an acceptable solution for use in a wide outdoor ambient temperature range.

Author Keywords: MV ASD (Medium Voltage Adjustable Speed Drive) HVAC (Heating Ventilation Air Conditioning)
MERV - Minimum Efficiency Reporting Value MERV

articleTitle: Long Cable Applications with PM Motors and MV Drives : Copyright Material IEEE Paper No. PCIC-2021-51
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Subsea Pump applications commonly use induction motors due to their rugged design and simple construction. However, such motors operate at low power factor and efficiency. These issues are minimized with Permanent Magnet Motors (PMMs) that operate at higher power factor and lower currents. Lower stator current is desirable because losses are an important factor with long umbilical cables between drive and motor. A PMM also allows an increased rotor gap reducing hydrodynamic drag on the motor and enabling higher shaft speeds. In this paper, operation of a mud line pump (MLP) coupled to a medium voltage PMM that is powered by a medium voltage (MV) drive over a 10.5 km cable length is presented. Motor starting and operation under load disturbances are investigated to show drive and motor performance. Waveforms showing steady state operation are presented to show benefits of the MV drive. The overall benefits of a PMM as compared with an induction motor based on operating experience are included.

articleTitle: EC 61850-Based Advanced Bus Transfer Scheme for Industrial Substations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In industrial power systems, supply power reliability is crucial to maintain process operations and ensure personnel safety. A Main-Tie-Main (MTM) residual bus transfer scheme effectively minimizes power system outages by quickly disconnecting a faulted source of power and transferring load to an available source, with minimal interruption during the transfer sequence. In industrial facilities such as refineries, many processes are supplied via motors. A variety of motors may be used: synchronous or induction, large or small. A transfer of supply power must be executed to avoid mechanical damage to motors and driven equipment. Utilizing traditional protection relays, the most efficient way to apply a MTM scheme is to use IEC 61850 GOOSE (Generic Object Oriented System Event) messaging for the inter-relay communications and control signaling. This technical paper discusses the advantages of a residual MTM automatic bus transfer scheme using IEC 61850 GOOSE messaging.

articleTitle: What Medium and High Voltage Stator Winding Partial Discharge Testing Can - And Can Not - Tell You
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Off-line partial discharge testing has long been used as a quality control test for the stator winding insulation in motors and generators rated 6 kV and above. Both on-line and off-line PD tests are widely used to assess the condition of the insulation to determine if maintenance is needed. Although there have been many papers published on successful PD tests where stator winding insulation problems were detected, this paper tries to point out some of the limitations of PD testing that we have learned over the years from over 18,000 machines. In particular, the issue of false positive indications and false negative indications is discussed, with several examples presented.

articleTitle: LNG Compressor Driver Trends Gas Turbines vs. Electric Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The Liquefied Natural Gas global market keeps expanding at a very fast rate enabling worldwide construction of large-scale liquefaction facilities with ratings previously thought impossible. Total liquefied natural gas trade reached historical high in 2016 and global liquefaction capacity keeps increasing with additional trains entering the construction phase also in 2016. This rapid increase in production capacities and capabilities requires, among other things, larger and more complex machinery with their corresponding technical and technological challenges, pushing the industry, especially equipment manufacturers, to search for viable options to satisfy operational requirements. Replacing traditional gas driven compressors with electric motor drives, at the sizes required for the application, has emerged as a trend aimed to simplify startup and increase efficiency while reducing emissions and life cycle costs. However, it has also created critical system design challenges which could have significant impact on plant performance and consequent production. Medium Voltage Synchronous Motors, controlled by Medium Voltage Adjustable Speed Drives, are leading the trend and have already been implemented in various projects. This paper discusses key areas and considerations pertinent to the liquefaction facility trend, including medium voltage motor and drive integrated application, focusing on minimizing risks at both the component and system levels

articleTitle: Advances in Solid-State Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Underwriters Laboratories (UL) listed solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs) are now being deployed for the first time ever. SSCBs eliminate the magnetic forces between phase conductors during short circuit events and do not require 1-2 cycles before clearing a short circuit. New silicon-carbide (SiC) semiconductors and current sensing methodologies mean SSCB’s interrupt short circuits faster than mechanical breakers. A SSCB can withstand millions more operations than traditional circuit breakers and achieves interrupting ratings of up to 200,000-amps. When a short circuit condition is sensed, nanosecond-speed SiC semiconductors first clear the fault and then open an internal air-gap mechanism, but yet, the air gap is never required to break the flow of current through air (i.e. no arc). The SSCB is software defined which means that their time current curves (TCC’s) are also software defined requiring fewer hardware stock keeping units (SKU’s). Other features include; remote control, revenue power metering, soft starting, virtual relaying, inherent arc flash mitigation, 60% size reduction, and far less maintenance than mechanical breakers.

articleTitle: Application and Control of Variable Speed Centrifugal Compressors in The Oil and Gas Industry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Centrifugal Compressors in the Oil and Gas Industry frequently use electric motors as drivers. Due to the high variability in process conditions users often specify variable speed electric motors, which allow the variation of the compressor speed over a wide range.The paper discusses the interaction between a centrifugal compressor and the process, and as a result, the control requirements for centrifugal compressor packages. The focus is on variable speed, upstream and midstream applications. The impact of the interaction between system characteristics and compressor characteristics, both under steady state and transient conditions, is explained. Also considered are concepts to optimize and control the units. Special attention is given to the specific speed-torque characteristics of variable frequency drive electric motors and variable speed hydrodynamic drives.Additionally, the impact of the process and how the process dynamics interact with the compressor is analyzed, categorized, and explained.

articleTitle: Potential Ignition Sources and Protections in Electric Rotating Machines Operating in Explosive Gas Atmospheres
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Electric rotating machines are the main prime movers to drive the necessary process equipment in the petroleum and chemical industries. Safety is a prime concern for personnel and processes. A breakdown can cause a loss of personnel and or revenue. As technology evolves, engineers continue to improve the design of these machines to be as safe as possible for the area in which they are selected for installation while also considering process criticality. This paper will discuss the different potential ignition sources in electric rotating machines and how they are designed, manufactured and protected to mitigate the risk of fire/explosion. The applicable regulations/standards are discussed for the various protection techniques adopted for each hazardous area classification. A brief overview of installation practices is also discussed.

articleTitle: New Motor Protection Standard IEEE 3004.8 – Getting Up To Speed!
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: IEEE Std 3004.8-2016 “Recommended Practice for Motor Protection for Industrial and Commercial Power Systems” is the first industrial-based standard providing detailed protection setting tables with companion single-line and three-line diagrams of recommended protection schemes for multifunction motor protection relays. Comprehensive motor protection information and diagrams are included for adjustable speed drive applications. The content triples and deepens the information from its predecessor IEEE Std 242-2001 (Buff Book) Chapter 10. Contributions were incorporated from end users, manufacturers, and consultants from across the world capturing advancements in protection technologies including field experiences. Updates include motor protection for hazardous (classified) locations. This paper covers a brief standard overview and deep-dives into material that is most applicable to the petrochemical industry.

articleTitle: Advantages of Real-Time Closed-Loop Simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Protective relays, controllers, and other hardware equipment can be connected to real-time simulation equipment for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation. These HIL real-time closed-loop simulations have historically been used in the aeronautics, space, defense, and utility industries. In this paper, the authors share their experience and best practices in applying HIL techniques for the petrochemical industry. The paper discusses best practices for constructing and validating models, connecting hardware to simulators, and running an effective HIL factory acceptance test. The authors highlight several in-service petrochemical projects that used HIL simulations and benefited from the resulting cost reduction and risk mitigation.

articleTitle: IEC VS. Ansi/Ul Medium Voltage Motor Control: Which one should you use and does it Matter?
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Most companies engaged In the OH, Gas & Chemicals sector have global operations. For simplicity commonality and increased reliability of operations and for economies of scale In procurement the companies prefer to buy common products across all operations. When It comes to medium voltage motor control centers, the issue of which standard to follow then becomes critical with the IEC and UL ones being most common. An increasing degree of commonality can be seen In these standards. It Is an opportune time to revisit the topic of whether It matters which set of standards Is followed. In this paper, we cover the key similarities and differences between UL 347 and the IEC 62271-1, -200 and -106 standards and see what the implications are for the applications seen in our industry. To-date, no such review Is available in published technical literature.

articleTitle: Led Lighting. Minimizing Ecological Impact without Compromising Human Safety
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Environmental requirements intended to protect wildlife from the effects of artificial lighting have been in place for quite some time. The light spectrum options available using traditional light sources meant compliance with these requirements was often challenging. More recently, LED technology can be customized to whatever light spectrum is required to meet the regulations.While the objective of the regulations is to protect wildlife, an unintended consequence is a potentially negative impact on worker safety. The light spectrum required in the regulations may not be appropriate for human vision to see well enough to effectively, and safely work in industrial facilities.With the color options LED offers, it is expected environmental wildlife regulations could be expanded with increased enforcement globally. The challenge for coastal and offshore petroleum operations will be to find a balance that meets these regulations without affecting worker safety.This paper will discuss the several regulations, available light sources and the need for appropriate action. Many standards aimed at reducing the negative ecological impacts that outdoor lighting systems pose are beginning to be updated and will eventually be enforced. Some of these standards are based on lighting design practices that are based on traditional light sources and have not considered the advantages of LED technology and may not adequately address wildlife issues or be at the expense human requirements for clear visibility at night.

articleTitle: What Should You Know Before Acquiring Partial Discharge on High Voltage Motors and Generators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Partial discharge monitoring is a useful diagnostic tool as it can expose problems that would be difficult to identify otherwise. However, evaluation of a single data point has always been difficult. A better option is to take periodic measurements, starting with a fingerprint or benchmark measurement on the new winding, to obtain trend data. Over the last decade, trend within the electric utilities, plants and petrochemical industries has been increasing to specify partial discharge limit when developing their technical specification for high voltage motors and generators. In response to that requirement, the motors and generators manufacturers may introduce cost by over-design, but this does not necessarily produce a machine with a longer life or increased reliability. The biggest challenge often observed during site inspections and testing is to carefully interpret the partial discharge data without causing unnecessary concern.In this paper, various case studies will be presented to facilitate the understanding of partial discharge and the implementation and measurement techniques that have evolved in the industry. In addition, data interpretation and recommended actions will be reviewed for when partial discharge is acquired at site under different loading and temperature conditions. Several site issues including improper cable routing, restricted airflow in the stator endwinding and surface contamination can aggravate partial discharge activity. To confirm elevated partial discharge due to aforementioned issues, individual case studies are presented systematically along with their respective remedial actions.

articleTitle: Battery Storage Applications in the Petrochemical Industry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: With increased research, usage, and production, the cost of battery storage technology has significantly decreased in recent years, to the point where real economic benefit can sometimes result. This paper begins by providing a primer on battery storage which includes a discussion of common battery technologies as well as a number of battery energy storage systems (BESS) grid applications. Next, a discussion of process uptime within a petrochemical facility will help show the importance of electrical grid reliability and how BESS might help provide critical grid stability. Finally, a theoretical case study where a BESS is installed for spinning reserve will be presented showing the economic viability of this emerging technology.

articleTitle: Cost-Benefit Analysis of Active Arc Mitigation Technologies in Low-and Medium-Voltage Switchgear : Copyright Material IEEE Paper No. PCIC-2021-53
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Maintaining a safe work environment while minimizing operational costs and downtime caused by accidental events is the key goal of distribution switchgear users. While major failure events such as arc flash are rare, when they do occur, the results can be catastrophic to both equipment and personnel and disrupt planned capital expenditures. There have been many advances in switchgear design and arc detection and mitigation technologies over the last two decades. These can be viewed on a spectrum of the upfront investment cost versus performance. This view ignores the differences among these technologies with respect to the disruption in operations and safety risks that they can mitigate. This is especially critical in process industries. This paper describes the technical characteristics and investment costs of all the available arc mitigation technologies. We then quantify the potential costs of operational disruptions and present an overall cost-benefit analysis for the technologies.

articleTitle: Electrical Circuit Protection and Switchgear Standards - ARC Flash, Monitoring and Relaying Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: With the compact space and environmental requirements of marine power applications, the design of circuit control and protection is particularly challenging. This paper will review the past, present and future trends that balance reliability and safety within the enclosed space of marine environments. Remote racking and automatic grounding devices that can mitigate at-risk behaviors will be analyzed. Cooling methods and the reliability of electrical connections will be evaluated. The paper will analyze safety, partial discharge, ground fault, loss of vacuum, and operational decision making that can result from collecting the data. In the case of the generator and main drive motors, the paper will analyze methods to eliminate background noise from partial discharge measurements.

articleTitle: Economics of Prefabricated Electrical and Instrumentation Buildings in Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The use of modular prefabricated buildings for the integration of electrical, instrumentation, and control systems equipment is an established practice in the industry. The concept of prefabrication has developed to the point that entire processing plants today are being fabricated in modules at dedicated facilities and shipped to the final project destination for reassembly. This paper discusses the economics of prefabricated electrical buildings in today's economy by looking at major factors that can affect the execution of large industrial projects: modular fabrication, method of transportation, shortage of skilled workforce, size for electrical enclosures and splits, type of enclosed equipment. The paper includes a comparison of a prepackaged power control building installation of a multiple split building with the installation of a large single piece building. The two approaches are compared in terms of risks, scheduled tasks, and estimated labor, to provide a framework for the execution of similar industrial projects in today’s economy.

articleTitle: Equipment Assemblies for Explosive Atmospheres
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper will discuss the requirements for evaluating an equipment assembly for evidence of compliance to applicable standards, for the purpose of obtaining certification or a listing from a Certification Body. This would allow the equipment to be marked as suitable for use in Explosive Atmospheres. Historically there was little guidance for evaluating equipment assemblies and as such evaluations could be complicated and costly. In 2017, a Technical Specification, IEC TS 60079-46, was published for the evaluation of Equipment Assemblies for Explosive Environments. In 2018, Canada adopted the document with Canadian deviations, as CAN/CSA C22.2 No.60079-46. It is likely the USA will also look at adopting a version of IEC TS 60079-46 with national deviations. This is a step forward in being able to approve assemblies so that any additional investigation in the field is minimized or eliminated.

articleTitle: Data Analytics - Optimization of Plant Operation Though Continuous Monitoring and Expert Level Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Many companies are beginning to embrace Data Analytics, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and digitalization with the intended purpose of optimizing maintenance practices. The ultimate objective is to increase revenue by reducing operating cost and maximizing production. Unfortunately, embracing IIoT and digitization in and of itself is not enough. To truly optimize plant operations via effective predictive maintenance practices, a holistic approach coupled with expert level analysis is necessary. The motor is the heart of the drivetrain system and through information gained by motor sensors, insight can be inferred on the operation of the entire drivetrain. It is only possible to enhance production and predictive maintenance by continuously monitoring all the data and then reducing the data with expert level analysis so that concise and actionable conclusions are presented to those responsible for plant operations.

articleTitle: Incipient Electric Circuit Failure Detection And Outage Prevention In Petrochemical Facilities Using Advanced Electrical Waveform Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Reliable and safe electric power is of critical importance in industrial facilities including field production facilities and plants. The best electric circuit protection and monitoring systems in use are not capable of failure prediction and incipient fault detection. Recent work demonstrates that early stages of apparatus, line, and cable failures can in some cases be detected and repaired, avoiding explosions and outages. The authors have developed a technology, which has become known as Distribution Fault Anticipation, which provides continuous health monitoring of circuits and real-time situational awareness of circuit activity. DFA monitors voltage and current signals to detect circuit abnormalities and failures. DFA utilizes intelligent algorithms to distinguish circuit events, including incipient failure signatures. This paper describes numerous examples of failing devices that were successfully detected, in early stages, thereby avoiding outages.

articleTitle: Medium Voltage Motor Vibration - Where do I Start? A Primer for Early Career Professionals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Petrochemical end users are hiring new graduates to fill in for the retiring workforce. Many universities have shifted the focus of their curriculums to cater to the field of high tech, leaving only a handful of institutions with strong programs in power engineering and subfields such as electric machines, power electronics, and power systems. Addressing skill gaps has become a point of discussion, from break rooms to board rooms. Electric motors form the bulk of prime movers for pumps, compressors, fans and other driven equipment. Proper application of electric motors ensures that a given service will be safe, reliable and efficient. Motor vibration is a critical application consideration. This paper outlines the principles of motor vibration, the electrical, mechanical, and civil reasons for their cause, and how vibration is detected and mitigated. Then, the paper describes factory acceptance testing and the governing standards (such as NEMA MG-1 and American Petroleum Institute (API 541)), and compares them from a vibration limit perspective. Finally, the paper discusses what manufacturing or external methods are effective in reducing vibration, and how rotors are balanced and tested to meet requirements. The goal of the paper is 1) to provide basic concepts and terminology related to medium voltage (MV) motor vibration and 2) to share an end user’s perspective on what matters most during specification, evaluation and installation.

articleTitle: A Practical Application of IEEE STD 1584-2018 : Copyright Material IEEE Paper No. PCIC-2021-54
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The IEEE Std. 1584-2018 Guide for Performing Arc-Flash Hazard Calculations presents new challenges in data gathering and equipment modeling due to the removal of the 125 kVA exception and the addition of the ability to model electrode configurations, enclosure dimensions, and bus gaps. Engineers must now understand equipment construction and choose whether to field measure equipment and use actual data, or use the typical values presented in IEEE-Std.1584-2018. This paper will discuss how incident energy (IE) and arc-flash boundary (AFB) are affected by electrode configuration, enclosure size and bus gap. This will be demonstrated for various equipment types to determine the practical impact of conservative assumptions. It will also discuss the implications of the new statement regarding arc sustainability at < 2000 A and provide suggested guidelines for the selection of electrode configuration based on examination of real-world equipment construction.

articleTitle: Run-Up Protection in High-Inertia Synchronous Motor Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: High-power salient-pole synchronous motors utilized in high inertia compressor applications in the air separation industry usually exhibit long starting times.During long asynchronous starts, there is a high thermal load induced in the rotor and motor protection becomes more challenging. Long starts are typically defined as run up times that exceed the permissible locked rotor time. The physical and mechanical limits of these motors and their influence on repetitive starts and waiting times are presented.A protection scheme based on current-time characteristics (thermal limit curves) is commonly applied.A general explanation of thermal limit curves and the benefits as well as the limits of these curves is given, for example the missing ability to display former heat impact and temperature distribution in different parts of the motor. An alternative timespeed based protection approach is presented.Experiences with practical motor protection, based on hundreds of operating motors, are shown. In addition, the topic of consecutive starts is discussed along with a method to better utilize the motor thermal capacity.

articleTitle: Introduction To Horizontal Directional Drill Installation Of High Voltage Transmission Lines And Other Duct Banks
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Horizontal Directional Drill (HDD) installation of High Voltage transmission has proven practical, and in some cases, less costly than traditional overhead options. Petrochemical facilities located on waterways provide excellent opportunities for underwater HDD installed transmission lines. These designs can provide significant safety advantages as well as improve system reliability. They eliminate height restrictions associated with overhead lines, reduce air traffic obstructions and reduce weather-related concerns typically associated with traditional overhead transmission lines, especially highly elevated transmission line crossings over waterways. They also offer significant opportunities when expanding existing facilities and designing for Prevention through Design by eliminating the overhead transmission lines and their associated contact risks throughout the life of the installation. Each HDD installed transmission line is different and can create significant challenges; however, the benefits associated with this technology can significantly outweigh the effort. This paper reviews some of the challenges associated with long high capacity transmission line installations along with their associated solutions as incorporated in previous projects. This paper does not cover smaller and shorter HDD installations typically associated with electrical distribution commonly used to cross streets, highways or feed commercial facilities.

Author Keywords: Soil Borings and Cone Penetration Testing

articleTitle: When to Replace aging Transformers Part-2
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Part-2 of when to replace aging transformers uses the initial case study to define basic problems surrounding transformers that were in service for more than 60 years. This document will provide an update on transformers returned to service, now 71 years old. It will expound more deeply on the insulation system, testing and criteria used to determine whether to allow a transformer to remain in service or to be replaced. It will explore the technique using Degree of Polymerization to assess remaining life of insulation as defined in the standards. With today’s information gathering techniques and data base manipulation, method of On-Line monitoring will be discussed. Additional information is published in paper titled "When to Replace Aging Transformers" at the 2010 IEEE PCIC Conference [3].

Author Keywords: LEL (Lower Explosive Limit) Oil Liquid Screen (OLS)

articleTitle: Application Considerations in View of New Revisions to High-Voltage Circuit Breaker Standards
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: IEEE recently introduced new revisions to the medium- and high-voltage circuit breaker standards. The revised standards provide for new ratings and capabilities; expand choices for users by making it easier to certify and accept under IEEE / ANSI standards equipment originally destined for the IEC market; and clarify the scope and limitations of various ratings of importance to the industrial user. This paper presents some of the more pertinent changes and how these changes affect the application of circuit breakers in the petroleum and chemical industries.

articleTitle: Lightning Protection at Petrochemical Facilities - Part 2 Requirements of Standards
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Development of lightning protection standards for petrochemical processing and storage facilities has progressed significantly over the past 20 years. Standard requirements have become more stringent and prescriptive. Understanding of development and propagation of lightning has grown with the advent of 3-D detection systems. This is Part 2 of a 3-part primer on lightning protection systems for petrochemical production, storage, and processing facilities. Part 1 - basic science and history. Part 2 - current requirements of national and international standards for protection systems at petrochemical facilities. Part 3 - alternative protection systems. The purpose of this paper, and the primer series, is to update the design and operating engineer’s knowledge of lightning protection at petrochemical facilities, and to increase the safety of these facilities to workers and equipment.

articleTitle: Electrical Best Practices and Lessons Learned from a Chemical Megaproject
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: A megaproject is summarized from feasibility design through commissioning and post start-up support from an electrical perspective. The project includes a 230 kV utility connection stepped down to a 69 kV substation that is connected to 21 modular substations for further distribution, internal generation integration, and load requirements of approximately 193 MW over 400 acres. Key lessons learned and best practices that are not covered in literature or industry standards are presented here. Topics include: 230 kV topology for grid connection, grounding and surge protection for high- voltage cabling, revised zone-selective interlocking schemes, power management system segregation and interfaces, preservation practices, protection relay setting management, new medium-voltage motor control center products, grounding and lightning protection, synchronous machine settings, adjustable speed drive control, and arc flash protection. The incorporation of lessons learned and best practices is important to maximize standardization, minimize site changes/re-work, and enable effective commissioning.

articleTitle: Using Multifunction Bus Differential Relays for CT Saturation Issues
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Current transformer (CT) saturation is a common issue in the world of power system protection. Typical switchgear design methodology is to size multi-ratio current transformers based on breaker rating. The ratios of instrument transformers are typically adjusted based on a feeder’s full load amps and cable ratings, primarily to provide more sensitive overcurrent set points and to provide a better metering range. However, lowering taps on the CT also reduces the ANSI class and rating, causing faster saturation and lower tolerance to fault currents. Switchgear space restrictions can limit the ability to install the desired CT class and rating, resulting in smaller CTs that will saturate under fault conditions. Low-impedance multifunction differential relays implemented with overcurrent protection provided a cost effective redundant solution that was used in a liquefied natural gas facility. Testing and modeling was completed and relay performance is presented.

articleTitle: Electrical Power Reliability Metrics for the Petrochemical Industry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Reliable electrical power is critical to the petrochemical industry. Power disruptions to petrochemical facilities have adverse safety, environmental, and economic impacts to the employees, surrounding communities, and businesses. To facilitate an understanding of the impact from electrical power events, this paper suggests a set of electrical reliability analytics with the intent of improving reliability through the reduction of process upsets and electrical power disruptions. This improvement in reliability can be achieved through a standardization of event and causal factor categorization along with capturing economic, environmental, and safety impact data.

articleTitle: Introduction to IEEE 841-2020 for Severe Duty Squirrel Cage Induction Motors - Up To and INcluding 370 KW (500 HP)
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: IEEE 841-2020 IEEE Standard for Petroleum and Chemical Industry – Premium Efficiency Severe Duty, Totally Enclosed (TEFC) Squirrel-Cage Induction Motors -Up to and Including 370 Kilowatt (KW) (500 Horsepower (HP)), to be issued in 2020 has been updated and improved from the 2009 version. The standard covers three-phase premium efficiency severe duty TEFC squirrel-cage induction motors with antifriction bearings in sizes up to and including 370 kW (500 hp). Important changes and updates have been made to the standard, including the addition of some applications for ASD motors in classified locations. Improvements to the standard are reviewed in detail. Requirements are identified that improve motor reliability and increase motor life.

articleTitle: Failsafe Motor Control Design to Prevent Runaway Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of key barriers to be considered when analyzing motor control designs in order to prevent runaway motors, especially runaway motor driven pumps against closed valves with the potential to lead to fire. A Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) is used to analyze typical motor control designs with the intent of determining a means of preventing a runaway condition due to failure of any one component. Following the determination of key barriers, the pipeline industry is surveyed to assess the prevalence of each barrier in similar operations and to look for additional best practices not previously documented. Conclusions are presented with final recommendations for consideration to avoid runway motors, especially those that drive pumps with the potential to run against closed valves, potentially leading to fire.

articleTitle: High Impedance Ground Fault Detection For A Safer Petrochemical Industry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper discusses the high impedance fault (HIF)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> detection system which utilizes relatively new technology on ground fault sensing and protection. The HIF system uses algorithms to detect a high impedance fault such as when a conductor falls onto the ground and where there is insufficient current to blow a fuse or operate a normal relay to trip a circuit breaker. The HIF detection system has potential for improving electrical safety in the oil patch where overhead power lines are prevalent and where present methods of ground fault detection are incapable of sensing and tripping for such a fault resulting in potentially dangerous conditions for workers and the general public. This paper introduces HIF detection to the petrochemical industry and presents the findings and conclusions of the author into the use of this relatively unique technology for the petrochemical industry.

Author Keywords: symmetrical components (positive sequence, negative sequence, and zero sequence)

articleTitle: Practical Approach to Developing A Model for ARC Flash and Power Systems Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In an ideal world, developing a model accurate enough to perform an arc flash and power systems analysis would be straight forward. Utilities would provide available fault current data that was accurate and not based on infinite bus values. A proper outage would occur with enough field time to collect all the data required. However, real world conditions may not allow the analysis to be done in an ideal way: the electrical equipment has nameplates that are worn down and impossible to read; single line diagrams might not be available; obtaining metering data to provide valuable operating load conditions might not be practical. Scope creep on every additional equipment discovery occurs. This list of real-world situations goes on and on. This paper explores the many cases of practicality involved with developing these models. It will discuss safety, detective work, Owner/Third party coordination, and assumptions that can be made to ensure a safe and reasonably accurate model.

articleTitle: Third-Party Certification - What Does it All Mean and How Does it Benefit The User?
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: For many electrical installations, the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) requires installed equipment to be Certified, Listed, or Labeled by a Recognized Certification Body, to show it is designed and tested for safe operation in the intended application. To comply with this and to assure that the equipment complies with the applicable design standards, customers specifications will require the equipment have a Third-Party Certification mark or label and may also require test verification by independent testing services. This paper will discuss the common terms, the purpose and the benefits of recognized certification programs and identify the potential issues when special testing is introduced or equipment modifications occur during factory and field testing.It will also discuss the obligations between the manufacturer, the certifier, and the end user of the equipment that are implied by entering into the certification process. Finally, it will attempt to answer the question; "Does the process chosen add the value that was expected?"

articleTitle: More Than Just a Box and Parts Design And Engineering Challenges Behind "db eb" Creations : Copyright Material IEEE Paper No. PCIC-2021-33
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In a hazardous area, where electrical equipment has been traditionally been stuffed into a thick-walled flameproof enclosure to provide explosion protection, different approaches have been introduced as alternatives to this concept. The approach of a series of small flameproof "d" enclosures, each with increased safety "e" terminations, commonly called a "db eb" component is not new, but the advantages provided have made a significant impact in industrial applications. While the concept is similar, a "db eb" component is not just a smaller version of the overall flameproof enclosure. The creation of the "db eb" product that allows for their integration into an increased safety "e" sheet metal or fiberglass enclosures is not as simple as creating a series of small flameproof "d" boxes that will enclose and protect the individual components.This paper will provide insight into the challenges that shape the engineering, production, and testing of the "db eb" components that are becoming more commonly used in hazardous location applications, including the USA and Canada. Unlike an overall explosionproof or flameproof, enclosure that provides the explosion protection, the design of these components can be quite challenging, but can really simplify the design of a system employing them and replace the overall flameproof enclosure.

articleTitle: Electrical Protection Standard Harmonization Challenges
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Information is presented that was learned during efforts to produce a harmonized electrical protection standard for global usage. Presented information details how a minor change, like where a differential relay is located, can impact not only the front layout of switchgear, but also; transformer specifications, Current Transformer (CT) requirements, internal switchgear layout and engineering design practices. Configuration choices and commonly selected auxiliary devices, such as mechanical lockouts, proved to have ties to location specific procedures or locally mandated codes. Differences, often realized only when cross-ocean standards were laid side by side, are presented along with the trail of consequences encountered when attempting to modify established alternate practices.

articleTitle: Case Study: Motor Fault Results in Zero-Sequence Current in Excess of Grounding Resistor Rating
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This case study involves the analysis of a phase-to-ground fault on one medium voltage motor that evolved into a phase-to-phase-to-ground fault involving a second motor. This fault scenario, commonly called a cross-country fault, then becomes more interesting when one of the motor contactor’s fuses blows, creating a cross-country fault that is back fed from a motor operating with an open phase. The waveforms captured during this fault provide valuable insight and exemplify the value in properly configured protective relay sequence of event recording. This paper explains how a low resistance grounded distribution system’s voltage response to a ground fault can cause a cross-country fault. The waveform analysis presented explains how to spot the signs of a cross-country fault and a motor with an open phase. It also explains how a zero-sequence current transformer can measure current in excess of the grounding resistor’s rated limit.

articleTitle: Reducing Risk (and Making Friends) with Proper Application of Electric Heat Tracing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Previous papers presented at the IEEE PCIC have covered certain aspects of Electric Heat Tracing (EHT) design, such as safety factors, process temperature consideration, sheath temperature, energy conservation, and safety. This paper will revisit several of these topics (and a few others) while covering several decades of lessons learned at a Canadian refinery.This paper will give suggestions of what to do, and what not to do, in hopes that it will provide designers and maintainers of EHT with useful information and tools to help apply EHT properly in new or replacement installations. It will also provide a few ways of dealing with existing high-maintenance installations.It should be recognized that several electrical standards now use the term Electrical Trace Heating or Trace Heating, instead of Electric Heat Tracing (EHT). These terms are used interchangeably within this paper.

articleTitle: Monitoring Devices and Design Considerations for Rotating Machines in Marine Duty Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: All rotating machines—including electric motors, generators, turbines, compressors, and others—benefit from and/or require the monitoring of the overall condition and health of the machine during its service. Typical monitoring parameters are temperature, vibration, power input or output (or both), lubrication, speed, and many more.This paper will discuss the above parameters from the perspective of what they are; why one must monitor them and how; and the advantages of what, why, and how.What devices are available and are used to monitor these parameters? and what are their inherent advantages and disadvantages, their usable limits, their input/output, etc.? In addition, the paper will discuss the recommended alarm and shutdown setpoints for each machine.The paper will also cover the monitoring requirement for the machine used in a marine environment and in hazardous areas. Finally, the paper will summarize, in a tabulated form for each machine, the parameters to be monitored and the instruments necessary to do so.

articleTitle: Low Voltage Motor Control Center Life Extention/ Safety Enhancement Projects - Analysis and Justification
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Defining the scope for a Low Voltage Motor Control Center (LVMCC) life extension/safety enhancement project requires the evaluation of several aspects. Included in these are: cost benefits, equipment condition, improved length of life, impact of the project on plant operation, and a reduction in hazards. An essential part of the value added is the reduction of the electrical hazards encountered performing the typical tasks called on by the facility while preserving operation.Over the past three years the solutions to extend systems life while improving safety has been fine tuned via several life extension projects in the field. The solution builds on the testing of LVMCC mitigation strategies reducing the hazard to an acceptable level for door open troubleshooting of individual motor starter cubicles published in 2013 through 2017.This paper focuses on the project justification of a tested and engineered solution for an asset management project that cost effectively extends the life of existing LVMCC.

articleTitle: Testing And Inspection Options for Squirrel Cage Induction Motors from Cradle to Grave
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide those who order, install, operate and maintain squirrel cage induction motors with a reference source of available inspection and testing options for motors throughout the construction, installation, operation, and maintenance cycle.

Author Keywords: installing electric motors and repairing electric motors

articleTitle: IEC/IEEE 80005-1:2019 Updates to Address Practical Issues with Installations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: IEC/IEEE Joint Working group (WG) members, under the leadership and guidance of the convener, put forward a tremendous effort to compose standards. Many meetings take place for consensus resolutions of the review comments. Authors of this paper are IEEE officers and WG members of this standard from the first issue through the present revised version and have knowledge of the history of comments and their resolution through the consensus process. This paper clarifies some of the requirements for the proper application of the standard. Authors are experienced in the design, installation, testing, and commissioning of shore power projects and provide their views of some of the issues that may require first-hand input to the industry professionals involved in these types of projects. Technical references and recommendations included in the paper should enhance reader’s knowledge of shore power projects mandated in numerous regions around the world to enhance safety of operators, minimize air pollution in the vicinity of Ports for health benefits and produce a cleaner environment for the public.

Author Keywords: shore to ship electrical protection system

articleTitle: Advances in Preventive Maintenance for Medium Voltage Equipment by Continuous and Remote Monitoring of Partial Discharge
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper is based on two decades of experience with continuous monitoring of Partial Discharge (PD) in medium voltage equipment. Simple and proven technology uses multiple sensors distributed along monitored objects. It allows for noise reduction and for localizing of PD activity sources. The importance of continuous PD monitoring vs. periodic PD measurements is discussed considering that PD activity can be very unstable and highly dependent on ambient conditions. Case studies from field experience including oil sands, refineries, chemical plants and off-shore platforms are presented to support the discussions. Advances in communication and computing have allowed Remote Continuous Monitoring to become a very effective combination for analyzing Partial Discharge patterns, relieving owners of the burden of data analysis for intricate (complex) PD diagnostics. Remote data collection is safe and secure, experts are readily available, and web portals can provide easy access to accumulated data.

articleTitle: Removing The Roadblock: Enhanced arc Flash Safety Using Integrated Primary Vacuum Fault Interruption and Secondary Sensing Systems on Transformers : Copyright Material IEEE Paper No. PCIC-2021-52
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Conventional primary fusing alone, while effective for protecting the primary of the transformer, is insufficient in protecting against arc flash dangers. This results in extremely high arc flash values on the secondary of the transformer through the secondary overcurrent protective device. Utilizing a combination of primary vacuum interrupting technology with secondary overcurrent sensing, arc-light sensing, and micro-processor-based relaying, allows secondary fault interruption response time to be significantly reduced, greatly decreasing incident arc energy in some cases by as much as 90%. Integrating this solution into a prefabricated and pretested piece of equipment offers drastically simplified arc flash modeling and equipment installation process, reducing the project timeline and risk of potential errors and complications in the field. Additionally, this technology can be used without the need to activate or engage other protective settings, delivering protection system simplicity and effectiveness to the user with minimal roadblocks or pitfalls. This paper outlines the theory, methodology, and implementation of an integrated transformer arc flash protection system for reducing the incident energy for secondary arcing events, thus, improving the safety of people working in close proximity to medium voltage transformers.

articleTitle: Totally Enclosed Water Cooled (IC 71W) Motors for API 541
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Well-designed totally enclosed water cooled (TEWC, IC 71W) motors provide considerably more power density and lower noise operation than other traditional totally enclosed motor types. API 541 does not allow for the use of TEWC motors. The intent of this paper is to show that TEWC motors should be added to the API 541 standard as an acceptable enclosure. This paper compares TEWC motors to totally enclosed designs allowed by API 541 and details how TEWC motors can be designed to meet the API 541 standard, which includes a 25-year service life requirement.

articleTitle: Operation of Large two Pole Sleeve Bearing Induction Motors with well Damped Resonant Speeds
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Rotor designs for two pole induction motors, especially those of larger size up to 5000 HP, exist in either "truly rigid" (operation below resonant speed) or "flexible" (operation above the first resonant speed) designs. API 541 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> edition (4.4.6.1.2) allows for a third mode of operation given specific criteria are met for a well damped resonant speed which can be of great benefit for adjustable speed drive applications where a speed lockout range is not acceptable. Test data and analytical models are presented and compared to differentiate between a "flexible" rotor design and a rotor design that operates with a well damped resonant speed.
